cilia from patients with primary ciliary dyskenesia syndrome have normal ultrastructure but disorientated beating pattern.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structure and function of cilia.
the study of the ciliary ultrastructure and orientation, the ciliary beat frequency and pattern and the mucociliary clearance of the nasal mucosa of patients with primary ciliary dysplasia.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of ciliary disorientation, in the absence of other ultrastructural defects, is sufficient to diagnose PCD.
ciliary disoriented patients have the clinical and functional features of PCD but the cilia have normal or near normal CBF.
ciliary disoriented PCD can exist as a distinct clinical entity, but the majority of cases of PCD are caused by a defect in ciliary ultrastructure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ciliary disorganization is the most common cause of PCD.
PCD can be defined as an ultrastructural abnormality of cilia that leads to a disordered ciliary beat pattern.
ciliary orientation is as important a factor for ciliary efficacy as ciliary structure and beat frequency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ciliary disorganisation is not a variant of primary cilial dyskinesia, it is a distinct condition that should be included in the list of primary ciliary diseases.
